sources_considered.why: An August 2025 investigation of a 400-account X network that used LLM-varied copypasta. It directly compares copypasta detection with LLM-varied text.
An October 2025 report on an AI-enabled X network that was first flagged partly because accounts shared the same content and identical hashtag strings.
The 2023 fox8 botnet study, which found LLM content classifiers failed while coordination signals worked. It falls before the target period and does not test copy-paste matching.
Finds that LLM rewriting of bot posts cut detector performance by up to 29.6%. It predates the target period and does not test duplicate-text matching.
Secondary coverage of Meta's behavior-based detection. It does not address copy-paste matching directly.

evidence_items.explanation: Investigators report that LLM-varied wording made a real network harder to catch than copy-paste networks, which are easily matched. This supports the mechanism. They still detected the network through account attributes and posting behavior.

evidence_items.explanation: A 2025 AI-enabled influence network on X was flagged partly because its accounts shared the same content and identical hashtag strings. Looking for duplicated content still helped expose a current operation.

unresolved_gaps: No systematic study was found that measures how often duplicate-text matching still catches recent AI-written campaigns.
The Citizen Lab network used AI mainly for images and video, not necessarily for per-post text, so it tests the claim only partly.
